newsitem.title: USA: UPS rivals seen deluged by service calls.
newsitem.headline: UPS rivals seen deluged by service calls.

text.p: Rivals of United Parcel Service were expected to be overwhelmed with service requests Monday morning after the Teamsters union went on strike againt UPS.
A Federal Express Corp worker in New York said orders were picking up, particularly at FedEx locations in central and lower Manhattan.
About 200,000 members of the Teamsters union began walking out on United Parcel Service of America Inc, the biggest U.S. shipping company, at midnight after contract talks broke down.
Fedex and other major UPS rivals reported substantial volume increases beginning last week. Several announced contigency plans in anticipation of a UPS work stoppage.
Most of the contigency plans called for a focus on handling a higher volume of requests from existing customers but not taking on large numbers of new accounts.

The FedEx worker in New York said her own office had seen only a modest increase in service requests this morning, but FedEx offices in midtown Manhattan and at the World Trade Center were "getting hit pretty bad."
FedEx employees expect to work double shifts throughout the UPS strike, the worker said. "We're going to be doing a lot of overtime this week," she said.
FedEx, which ordinarily handles about 2.8 million packages a day, said it would not open any new accounts until the UPS labor situation had been resolved. FedEx is the industry No. 2 behind UPS.
Industry experts say UPS rivals will not be able to make up for UPS's absence. UPS ordinarily handles about 12 million parcels daily and ships more than all its competitors combined.
